doc.title: Arthur Baron interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 3, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]

chapter: Deaths and the state of the country
title: Hal Willner and the Mingus project 'Weird Nightmare'
summary: Baron recalls Hal Willner and his arrangement of 'Eclipse' with Partch instruments and Leonard Cohen on the Mingus tribute.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Yeah. You know? Oh my God. And so I tell you, when Bucky passed, right around the same time the wonderful producer Hal Willner — do you know who he was?

I did a lot of projects with him. My first project with him was an amazing project of doing Mingus. It was called “Weird Nightmare: Meditations on Mingus.” And I arranged a piece on that, on “Eclipse” in a totally different fashion, not about a black and white person in a couple, but about the first time mankind ever saw an eclipse, cavemen. And we had all these Harry Partch instruments, I played didgeridoo, all kinds of — and he actually got Leonard Cohen to recite some poetry, just a part of a poem that Mingus wrote, “The Chill of Death.” Hal was always creating unbelievable groups of people. And you know that’s when I got mad at the powers-that-be, and you know who I’m talking about, that those deaths didn’t need to happen.
